_note: Household work bought and cooked food bought (Complaint 645). A domestic servant's hour stands for the household work another household would otherwise do with its own hours (data/world/household_work.json). A cooked meal is what a cook or an eating house turns out for a household that has no hearth of its own. Sizes are estimates of the work, confidence D.

domestic_service_hour.basis: per hour of household work done for another household
domestic_service_hour.yield_basis: An hour of a servant's work does an hour of household work: the need counts hours (data/world/needs.json, household_work), so one hour gives one unit. Confidence D: a servant is taken to work at the pace of the household member whose hour she replaces.

cooked_meal_kg.basis: per 1000 kg of cooked pottage or stew
cooked_meal_kg.yield_basis: A pot of meal and vegetables boiled in water: 300 kg of flour and 200 kg of vegetables with 500 kg of water make about a tonne of pottage (mass balance: 300 + 200 + 500 = 1000, the water of boiling and the water in the vegetables roughly cancelling; no source found, conf D). Heat: bringing a tonne of mostly water to the boil from cool takes about 0.3 MJ a kilogram, and an open hearth delivers about a tenth of the fuel's heat to the pot, so about 3 MJ of thermal heat a kilogram (author's estimate, conf D), priced through the thermal_mj market. Labour: cutting, stirring and serving, about 40 hours to a tonne (author's estimate, conf D). Calories: the satisfaction factor in data/world/needs.json is the food of the ingredients over the mass of the meal, (300 * 1.0 + 200 * 0.1) / 1000, so cooking adds no food energy.
